cohort: The study included 2,864 pregnant women (67 with isolated hypothyroxinemia, 784 euthyroid in the first trimester; 70 with isolated hypothyroxinemia, 1,943 euthyroid in the second trimester) whose thyroid hormone concentration was examined.
finding: Isolated hypothyroxinemia during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy does not significantly increase the incidence of adverse maternal outcomes and perinatal complications.
cross-section timing: First and second trimesters of pregnancy for thyroid hormone concentration measurement
